steps.body: To compare two candidate lines, look at the **gaps** between the dots and each line — these gaps are also called residuals. The better fit has smaller gaps overall — the dots huddle closer to it. Bigger gaps mean a worse summary of the trend. For now, judge closeness by eye; a precise rule for comparing residuals comes later.
Judge a fit by the residuals, not by the eye.

widget.prompt: Fit a line to these four points. Aim to leave as little gap as possible above and below.
widget.successFeedback: y = 2x + 1 passes through every point exactly. A good fit is not the line that looks nice — it is the one that leaves the smallest gaps, and here the gaps close to nothing.
widget.slopeFeedback: The steepness is off: the points climb 2 for every 1 across.
widget.offsetFeedback: The steepness is right but the line sits too high or too low. At x = 0 the pattern is heading for y = 1.

predict.prompt: Study how the points spread as x grows. Will the best-fit line slope UPWARD, DOWNWARD, or lie flat?
predict.reveal: Rising points mean a positive association — the line that hugs them must climb too. Flat is tempting when wide vertical scatter makes a cloud look shapeless, but the fit still tilts with the drift — flat only wins when there is no drift at all. Direction comes before any exact slope.

cml.actionGoal: Move a fitted line and coordinate association, residual balance, prediction, and model limitations.

steps.body: A tightly clustered cloud can be summarized by a line with very small gaps — a strong fit. A widely spread cloud leaves bigger gaps no matter how you draw the line, so even the best line is a looser summary.

explanationVariants: A tightly clustered cloud lets a line fit with small gaps — a stronger fit than a spread-out cloud allows.
Tighter clouds allow closer-fitting lines; spread-out clouds don't.

widget.prompt: Cloud X's dots hug a straight path tightly; Cloud Y's dots are widely spread. Whose best-fit line will have smaller gaps?

options.label: Cloud X — its dots are tightly clustered
options.feedback: Right — a tight cloud lets the line fit with small gaps.

options.label: Cloud Y — it has more dots to average
options.feedback: Spread-out dots leave BIGGER gaps — the tight cloud (X) fits more closely.

options.label: They will be equal
options.feedback: The tight cloud (X) allows smaller gaps than the spread one (Y).

options.label: Neither has gaps
options.feedback: Real clouds have gaps; the tight one (X) has smaller ones.

widget.prompt: Sort each described line by how well it fits its cloud.

items.label: dots huddle tightly along the line
items.feedback: The dots sit close to the line, so the gaps are small — that closeness is what makes a good fit.

items.label: line runs the wrong direction from the cloud
items.feedback: A line sloping opposite to the cloud's trend pulls away from the dots as you follow it, so the gaps grow — that makes it a poor fit.

items.label: roughly equal dots above and below, all close
items.feedback: Balanced above and below with small gaps means the line runs through the middle — a good fit.

items.label: most dots sit far to one side of the line
items.feedback: When nearly all dots fall on one side, the line isn't centered in the cloud, and those large one-sided gaps make it a poor fit.

widget.missFeedback: Not quite — good fits are close AND balanced; poor fits have big gaps or the wrong direction.
widget.successFeedback: All sorted — closeness and balance make a good fit.

explanationVariants: Adding up how far the dots sit from the line measures the fit: smaller total distance is better.
The total distance from dots to the line is the quality measure — smaller is better.

widget.prompt: What single idea best measures how good a line of best fit is?

options.label: How far the dots sit from the line overall (their residuals)
options.feedback: Right — smaller total distance from the dots, judged informally as their residuals, means a better fit.

options.label: How many dots the line touches
options.feedback: Touching dots isn't the measure — it's the overall CLOSENESS of all dots to the line.

options.label: How steep the line is
options.feedback: Steepness is the slope, not the fit quality — closeness of the dots is.

options.label: How long the line is
options.feedback: Length doesn't measure fit — the total distance from dots to the line does.

explanationVariants: Even with small gaps, a line with all dots on one side isn't centered — balance is part of a good fit.
A good fit is both close AND balanced above/below.

widget.prompt: A line stays close to the dots but has every dot slightly above it. How could it improve?

options.label: Shift it up so dots are balanced above and below
options.feedback: Right — nudging it into the middle balances the cloud.

options.label: Make it steeper
options.feedback: Steepness isn't the issue — it needs to move UP to balance the dots around it.

options.label: Make it longer
options.feedback: Length doesn't fix balance — shifting it up to center the dots does.

options.label: Leave it — closeness is all that matters
options.feedback: Balance matters too — all dots on one side means it should shift up.

steps.body: Pick the better of two lines.
explanationVariants: The line with dots split evenly above/below and small gaps beats one that's close but leaves all dots below it.

widget.prompt: Line P: dots split evenly above and below, all fairly close. Line Q: also close, but every dot sits above it. Which fits better?

options.label: Line P — close AND balanced
options.feedback: Right — P is both close and balanced, the mark of a good fit.

options.label: Line Q — it's under all the dots
options.feedback: Being under every dot means Q isn't balanced — P (balanced and close) fits better.

options.label: They fit equally well
options.feedback: P is balanced above and below; Q is not — so P is the better fit.

options.label: Neither fits
options.feedback: P fits well — close and balanced; Q is close but unbalanced.

hints: Both lines are close, so use the second test: balance.
P has dots evenly split above and below; Q has all dots above it.
Balanced beats unbalanced, so Line P is the better fit.

steps.body: Judge a fit by closeness and balance: small gaps, dots split evenly above and below.
takeaways: Smaller total distance from dots to line means a better fit.
A good line is also balanced — dots split above and below.
Tight clouds allow closer fits than spread-out clouds.
steps.teaser: Next: choosing the best line's equation.

concept.body: Judge a line of best fit by closeness (small gaps between dots and line) and balance (dots split evenly above and below). Smaller total distance means a better fit.

explanationVariants: The line whose dots hug it more tightly (smaller gaps) is the better fit.
Smaller gaps between dots and line means a better fit.

widget.prompt: Line A's dots hug it closely; Line B's dots are far from it. Which fits better?

options.label: Line A
options.feedback: Right — closer dots (smaller gaps) means a better fit.

options.label: Line B
options.feedback: Farther dots is worse — Line A, with smaller gaps, fits better.

options.label: Equal
options.feedback: Line A's dots are closer, so it fits better.

options.label: Neither
options.feedback: Line A fits better — its dots are closer.
